images.title: 3375 splits into three equal groups
images.purpose: Shows the prime factors of 3375 split into three identical groups of 3 × 5, so 3375 = 15 × 15 × 15.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. The number at the top, three identical rows of prime tiles in the middle, and one equation below.
images.exact_structure: At the top centre: 3375 in large dark digits. Below it, exactly 3 identical horizontal rows of round tiles, each row exactly 2 tiles reading 3 and 5. Top row filled teal (#0072B2), middle row amber (#E69F00), bottom row reddish purple (#CC79A7), each tile directly under its match. Six tiles in all. Below the rows, centred: 15 × 15 × 15. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number is a perfect cube when its prime factors split into three identical groups.
images.description: Shows the prime factors of 3375 split into three identical groups of 3 × 5, so 3375 = 15 × 15 × 15.

image_decisions.why: Three matching rows of prime tiles make the grouping test and the cube root visible together.
